Bare, early spring. No hull, cabin or shore line goes with these strokes.

entities.note: SECOND PASS (west): recorded by nobody (merge notes, seam S4b: 'a willow crown hangs from beyond the silk's top edge at 15200-15570, v 15-70, with no trunk on the silk: recorded by nobody'; t1 left the same strokes to river_w as 'a faded boat or ripples'). Strokes: a fan of 6-8 parallel curved whips converging at (15490-15500, 20-33) and spreading down-east to (15540-15567, 50-70); more whips west of the seam at 15380-15463, v 17-50 belong to S4b's far-bank trees (S4b.tree.far_bank_15308, crown_e (15392, 40)) or to this crown. Below v 75 the silk is plain from 15480 to 15750 (no hull, no shore ink). BASE est: S4b's far-bank ground S4b.grd.far_bank_15330 names, in its note, a willow foot at about (15520, 70) est with no entity; I take that point, so the main point is on S3's side by 20 px. The lead may give it to S4b as its third far-bank tree (then it is a seam note here). OTHER READINGS: (a) the tile restyle paints an arched mat roof here, as the after part of S4b's small cabin boat (S4b.veh.boat_small_cabin_15182, stern_top (15460, 78)): the scan has no hull under the strokes, so not a boat; (b) the east end of S4b.tree.far_bank_15308's crown: then drop this entity and set that tree's crown_e to (15570, 70). Crops: c_topcrown.jpg, insp_topcrown.jpg, c_topseam.jpg, o_topseam_s4b.jpg. FRAME AGENT (second pass accepted): kept as S3's by its main point; it stands on S3.grd.far_bank_seam_15500, the strip that joins S4b's far bank (S4b.grd.far_bank_15330) to the silk's top edge (frame step). If the lead gives it to S4b, it becomes a seam note here.

Crops: c_heap.jpg, insp_heap.jpg, c_hall_m.jpg.

entities.name: narrow empty skiff under the arch's south foot
entities.what: A long, narrow, empty skiff lying in the water under the south half of the arch, parallel to the south bank: a slim hull seen side-on, about 340 px long, its sharp west end running in behind the arch's south leg and its east end rising to an upturned stem with a small knob on its tip; four short uprights (frames or thwarts) stand between gunwale and bottom over its east half. No crew, oar, pole or mooring line is painted.
entities.vis: part: its west end runs in behind the arch's south leg (u ~18915-18935); the south-east end post crosses it at u ~19015
entities.note: SECOND PASS (middle): replaces floating_timber_19090 (retired at the second pass) (edit below: retire it). Strokes on contrast crops at zoom 3-4: gunwale (top line) (18933, 947) -> (19014, 964) -> (19100, 975) -> (19160, 975) -> (19252, 945); bottom (18933, 961) -> (19014, 983) -> (19100, 1000) -> (19160, 997) -> (19255, 967). The depth grows from ~14 px in the west to ~25 px at u 19100-19160, then both lines rise together into a stem whose tip carries a small knob at (19250-19260, 943-952), with a short post down to (19258, 965). Uprights between the lines at u 19108-19113, 19160-19170, 19185-19192 and 19210-19215 (v ~970-1000). This is a hull's profile: a log or spar keeps one depth along its length and has no rising stem. BOW: the upturned stem is east, so front = the waterline under it; the west end is sharp and hidden, rear est where the two lines meet behind the arch's leg. pose 'moored' is a reading: nothing ties it and nobody is in it; it lies ~40-60 px north of the south bank's est shore (v ~1040), under the ridge of S3.bld.mat_shed_19160. OTHER READINGS, kept: a long timber or spar afloat (river_e's first reading), or a footing timber of the bridge's south abutment (river_e); neither explains the stem with its knob. t7 and the bridge agent also read a skiff. OWNER: its main point (front, u 19255) falls in the east range; the merge listed it for the middle pass. SCALE CUE: hull ~340 px long (4.4 m at 77 px/m), ~20-25 px deep. Crops: scratchpad/S3_second_middle/i_timber.jpg, i_timber_e.jpg, i_timber_w.jpg, i_timber_m.jpg.

entities.name: slatted panel at the west stall's north-east corner
entities.what: A short panel of two rails with slanting slats between them, about 85 px long, standing at the north-east corner of the west mat-awning stall between the man seated on the bench (west of it) and the round-faced youth (east of it): a rack, a ladder set down, or a bench's slatted back.

entities.vis: part: its foot is behind the seated man's knees
entities.note: SECOND PASS (middle): the merge's item 'the west railing piece'. Accept only together with the edit on S3.str.rainbow_bridge that removes its custom points rail_w_piece_s/rail_w_piece_n (the same strokes); if the lead keeps the bridge's reading, decline this. Strokes (raw and stretched crops at zoom 3-4): two rails from (18593, 390) down to (18640, 457), long axis slope +1.4 (falling to the east), 4-5 slats between them at (18605-18632, 395-465). Why not the deck's west railing: (1) it stands 590-670 px west of deck_e at the same v, but the water's edge runs 700-775 px west of deck_e all along the ramp (reviewed item 'deck entities'), and the man seated on S3.prop.bench_18630 sits between it and the water, so it is inside the deck, not on its edge; (2) a stretch of the west railing would run parallel to the near railing, rising to the east (slope -1.4 to -2.0 on the south flank), while this panel falls to the east; (3) it is 85 px long against the near railing's ~50 px height at the crown. So it is no evidence for deck_w. Group: the lead adds it to S3.grp.west_stall_18330. Crops: scratchpad/S3_second_middle/d_frame_raw.jpg, d_west_rail.jpg, d_west_rail_z4.jpg.
